title: Nizhny Novgorod
capsule: The Principality of Nizhny Novgorod-Suzdal emerged as a distinct entity in 1341 when Konstantin Vasilyevich separated it from the Vladimir-Suzdal lands, establishing his capital at Nizhny Novgorod—founded by Yuri II of Vladimir in 1221 at the strategic confluence of the Volga and Oka rivers. Under Dmitry Konstantinovich (r. 1365–1383) the principality briefly rivalled Moscow for regional primacy in northeastern Rus'; Dmitry signed peace agreements with Grand Prince Dmitry Donskoy of Moscow in 1366 and 1374, and the two states fought intermittently for Volga trade-route dominance. Moscow's Prince Vasily I secured a Horde yarlyk (patent) in 1392 and annexed the principality through political pressure and dynastic maneuvering, with final resistance extinguished by 1395.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's existence and capital are documented in Russian chronicles; precise outer boundaries in the Volga-Oka interfluve region are not delineated in surviving medieval sources and remain approximate.
